newsitem.title: USA: Lilly, Synaptic say expand research pact.
newsitem.headline: Lilly, Synaptic say expand research pact.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co and Synaptic Pharmaceutical Corp agreed to expand the size of their collaboration focused on the discovery and development of serotonin receptor drugs, the companies said.

At the same time, Indianapolis-based drug giant Lilly said, "In an unrelated move, it was disclosed that, as part of Lilly's ongoing asset management strategy, it had sold its shares in Synaptic earlier this year."
Lilly had owned as many as 525,721 shares of Paramus, N.J.-based Synaptic, equal to about 7.2 percent of outstanding shares, Synaptic said.
Lilly has sold all the shares, Synaptic said.
Synaptic said it was the first to discover seven of the 14 known human serotonin receptors, or sites in the nervous system where the neurotransmitter serotonin is received.
The company said it has received U.S. patents covering four of these receptors.
Additional patent applications covering these and other serotonin receptors are pending, Synaptic said.
Synaptic has licensed certain of its serotonin receptors to Lilly on an exclusive basis for discovery and development of drugs for the treatment of serotonin-related disorders.
The expansion of the collaboration calls for Lilly to fund additional scientists at Synaptic working on additional serotonin receptors, the companies said.

Under the original agreement, Synaptic will get payments upon achievement of certain development milestones, as well as royalties on product sales. Additionally, Lilly's research funding to Synaptic will continue through December 31, 1998.
